# dsh-workspace-status
English · 中文
Sidebar upgrades for DeepSeek Harness:

1. **Workspace status marks** — colored status on the workspace (folder) row:
waiting for you, runni

ng, and just finished, aggregated from the sessions
inside it.
2. **Pinned conversations section** —

conversations pinned through the shipped
pin action leave the regular workspace groups and appear i

n a dedicated
section above the browsing region, grouped per workspace with the same
header treatmen

t and a pin icon on every row.
3. **Pinned notifications** — when a pinned conversation starts waiti

ng for
you or finishes unread, the plugin can raise a desktop notification (when the
window is in th

e background) and always shows an in-app notice in the pinned
section. Bell and chime toggles sit in
the section header.

Harness draws a status dot on every conversation row, but nothing on the
workspace row above it. Col

lapse a group, or scroll it out of view, and the
folder cannot tell you that an agent inside is stuc

k waiting for an approval or
still working. This plugin gives the folder row the same kind of mark.
| Mark | Meaning | Color |
| solid dot | at least one session is waiting for you — approval, plan review, or an answer | amber

(`--dsw-alias-state-warn-primary`) |
| stroked ring, spinning | at least one session is running, inc

luding a running subagent | blue (`--dsw-static-deepseek-450`) |
| solid dot | at least one session
finished recently and has not been opened since | green (`--dsw-alias-state-success-primary`) |

The mark sits in the empty right-hand end of the workspace row — the same place
a session row puts i

ts timestamp — and does not displace the title. It appears
for expanded and collapsed groups alike,

The bell in the Pinned header (next to the count) controls notifications; the

## How it works

- The mount is an entry in the additive `sidebar.footer.action` seat. It
publishes a stylesheet, a v

isually hidden activity description, and a portal
anchor; it adds no control of its own at the foot.

- Workspace marks read the same public data the browser uses: `useWorkspaces`
(`items`, `archivedSe

ssionIds`, `pinnedSessionIds`), `useSessions` (`byId`) and
`useSessionStatus` (`running`, `pendingIn

teraction`, `completionUnread`).
- The workspace mark is the folder row's trailing pseudo-element, e

mitted as a
rule targeting `[data-row-key="workspace:<id>"]::after`.
- The Pinned section is rendere

d through a React portal into a container
inserted immediately before the sidebar's `regionArea` ele

ment. The official
browser is not replaced: search, menus, drag ordering, dialogs and directory
pick

ing stay native.
- Pinned rows are lifted by hiding their `[data-row-key="session:<id>"]` rows
with

generated CSS (`display:none!important`); search-result rows carry no
`data-row-key`, so they remain

visible.
- Unpin calls `ctx.workspaces.unpinSession(id)`; opening a pinned row calls
`ctx.uiWorkspa

ce.openSession(id)`. The pin set itself comes from the
Workspace snapshot, so both the official tree

and this section stay in sync.
- Collapse memories and notification preferences live in browser
`lo

calStorage`; no plugin settings are written. Notification delivery uses the
renderer's standard `Not

oving the plugin removes the mount, the stylesheet and the inserted
section container; no profile or
session data is changed by the plugin.
## Compatibility

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` (developed and verified against
`0.2.1-rc.3`); Web and De

sktop clients.
- Node `>=22.18.0` for the build-free package and its tests.
- No host-side services,

no settings, no model-visible tools or prompt changes.
